cities.d: The capital and cosmopolitan centre of the country, although with few standout sights.

x.around: Many taxis do not use a flat rate, you negotiate a price in advance. Short distance inside city can be 80 som. A taxi for a day can be negotiated. An hour drive to mountain costs about 1,100 som while getting back is usually much more expensive because the driver has to run twice without passengers since during your stay he needs to return to the city to work.

hidden.d: You can buy tickets from the ticket office around the side. There's a sauna, ice-cold pool, and for an extra 200 som an attendant will lather you up, scrub you and then hose you down.
General Mikhail Frunze (1885-1925) was a World War I and civil war general born in Bishkek, of such renown that the city was named for him until independence.
A large square with monument and eternal flame to commemorate the victory against Nazi Germany in WWII.
A children's theme park. While this park may be in need upkeep and renovation, it's a great look into the past when Kyrgyzstan was a part of the Soviet Union.

x.intro: Bishkek (Бишкек), the capital and largest city in Kyrgyzstan, sits at the foothills of the Tien Shan mountain range in the Chui Valley. It is a relatively new city with few historical sites, but it makes a great place to start your trips to the mountains and alpine lakes of the Tien Shan.

must.d: The main city square is a vast expanse of concrete that ceased to be called Lenin square in 1991, and is the site of frequent political demonstrations and regular festivals.

Three floors: the bottom floor covers prehistoric times to the beginning of the 20th century, and the second displays events of the Communist era. The top floor showcases the history and culture of the Kyrgyz people.
Exterior of dazzling white and blue, the interior is cluttered by scaffolding as the cupola frescoes are refurbished.
Gallery of local art in three sections: local representational art particularly by Turusbehov, Stakhanovite glories of tractors in the steppes, and modern art.

n.de: Nationales Museum für bildende Künste Gapar Aitijew
n.it: Museo Statale di Belle Arti "Gapar Aitiev"

next.d: major city of Kazakhstan which is situated not so far away

x.safe: Inside clubs, keep a cool head and stay aware of your surroundings. Most clubs have security staff, but remain vigilant regardless. Do not leave belongings unattended on the table while you dance. Take particular care in the taxi area outside clubs late at night, where opportunistic theft can occur, and do not expect much assistance from club security if something is stolen.

cities.d: The gateway to Issyk Kul lake. A small, dying industrial centre on the western shore, and a former fishing town, with a train service from Bishkek through a beautiful passant Chui Valley.

x.intro: Balykchy (Балыкчы) is a city of 51,000 people (2021) at Issyk Kul. It was the center of the lake's fishing fleet, but has suffered a major decline since the collapse of the Soviet Union. It now only on the path to the tourist sites of the lake, but largely by-passed.

cities.d: One of the gems of Issyk Kul, this was originally a Slavic settlement with a wealth of hiking, outdoor and sports available, including the Altyn Arashan hot springs, Karakol Canyon, and the beautiful…

x.around: Important lines: * 101: Zhamansariev Str. - Toktogula - Lenin street - Kapacaeba - Masaliev Str. down to the entrance of the Karakol Gorge (10 som) * 102: Zhamansariev Str. - Toktogula - Gebze - Salieva * 350: Zhamansariev Str.

hidden.d: Nikolay Mikhailovich Przhewalsky was one of the first Russian geographers who started studying in detail the geography, flora and fauna of the Central Asia.
Early on Sunday mornings one of Kyrgyzstan’s biggest animal markets takes place around 2 km north of central Karakol.

Issyk-kul Central Mosque of Karakol city named after Ibrahim Aji was built by initiative of Ibrahim Aji. He invited the famous Beijing architect Chou Seu and 20 carvers with the skills of traditional Chinese architecture and…
In July 1869, when Karakol was a garrison town on the edges of the Tsarist Russian Empire, the first church was built here.

A beautiful rock formation besides an ageing sanatorium, 35 km west of Karakol and south of the Jeti Ögüz village. This and many other sights can be found on the way to or from Karakol around Issyk Kul—see the region article.
The museum is housed in a pretty chocolate-box cottage in central Karakol. It was the pre-revolutionary summer home of the Iliana merchant family.

x.intro: Karakol (Каракол) is a city in Kyrgyzstan on the east of Lake Issyk Kul.

next.d: A remote and empoverished eastern village quickly becoming popular as a winter and hiking destination. Take bus 331 to "шахта" from the main bazaar at 08:30, 13:30, 17:30. 80 som.
Proper buses (not marshrutkas) to Bishkek leave at 20:00 and 21:00 from the backside of the bus station and cost 330 som (arriving in Bishkek the next morning at 05:30-6:00).
Has many interesting and must-see destinations that can easily be reached by public transport or autostop from Karakol.

n.en: Issyk Kul and the Tian Shan

x.safe: Unfortunately unemployment and the resulting alcoholism have left a toll, as many young people have left, and the soaring crime rate has made it rather dangerous at night.

cities.d: A small village with a park containing various Soviet structures, and a local animal bazaar, as well as an entry of point for Song Kul and launch pad for treks up into the Tian Shan Mountains.

x.around: Kochkor is a large village, but can be easily explored on foot. However, if you want to visit a nearby village, finding a taxi might be difficult. The best thing to do is walk in the direction you want to go and wave at a passing car if you want them to stop. If they do give you a ride, it is polite to offer them money for petrol.

hidden.d: This community-based organisation has the biggest network throughout the country.
A haven of greenery just south of the taxi stand. Within the park are various Soviet-era structures in various stages of use.
Here you can view Kyrgyz livestock and observe local farmers buying and selling their animals. The bazaar is also a good place to stock up on any essentials that you might be running low on.
Another professional tour organizer with a homestay in Kyzart village (20 km west of Kochkor).

next.d: A scenic and very remote lake nearby. Horseback riding is very popular, but a strain for you body. If needed tours can be arranged in town. But (hitch)hiking is also possible.
One of the highlights of Kyrgyzstan. You need to get to Naryn first.
A village popular with foreign tourists, has beautiful orange mountains around it and a mountain valley for hiking and yurt stay. Also gateway to the western regions of Kyrgyzstan.

cities.d: A city in the Tian Shan, near Lake Song Kul, the gateway to the entire southeastern region, its ruins, mountains, and high alpine lakes.

x.around: Shared taxis are a convenient way to get around. On the main road, taxis are treated like marshrutkas, meaning people get on and off. As of August 2015, the fare for a ride is a mere 10 som, but can be 20 som if you want to go all the way back to the bridge. Do not pay more!

hidden.d: This is quite the edifice with all the blue tile on the facade and minaret. Like the ones in Bukhara and Samarkand, or at least it takes one back to there.

x.intro: Naryn is a city in southeastern Kyrgyzstan in the region of the same name.

next.d: Instead of heading back to Bishkek and from there to Osh, you might choose to go directly to Jalal-Abad, a convenient transport hub. This can be much faster but certainly not cheaper.

cities.d: Kyrgyzstan's second largest city, a fascinating, 3,000-year-old Ferghana Valley market town.

x.around: Taxis are cheap, a ride from the city to the airport is about 300 som.

hidden.d: Basic collection of Soviet realist pieces along with some regional Kyrgyz works.

n.en: Turgunbai Sadykov Osh Regional Museum of Fine Art

hidden.d: Interesting Islamic architecture at base of Mount Sulaiman, named after King Suleiman’s vizier.

If you feel like exploring, you can drive about 3.5 hours south of Osh to the Alai (Alay) Valley for spectacular views of the Alai Range to the northwest and north and the Pamir Range, particularly Lenin Peak, to the south.
Statue of Kyrgyz freedom fighter against Soviet rule.
A waterfall where a subterranean river emanates from the cliff in a tight mountainous canyon. About 3 hours from Osh.
Said to be oldest mosque in Osh, a tribute to 16th-century Rabat Abdul Khan. Non-Muslims most likely not allowed entry.
Blue and white church with a stone gate in front stemming from the early 20th century that is supposedly the only Russian church left in Osh after the demise of Soviet Union and events that followed.
A mosque of notable statue with blue mosaic tiles that you can see before going up Mt Sulaiman. Tourists not really allowed in though.

x.intro: Osh is a city in the Ferghana Valley of Kyrgyzstan. The city is at least 3,000 years old and today remains a lively place.

must.d: A mountain looming over the city full of ancient sites of worship, some still in use, dating back several millennia.
A nature reserve on the north face of the Alay Range. Established in 1992, but not developed. Hiking and sightseeing will require some planning, or possibly arranging a trip through a guide (e.g.

n.en: Kyrgyz Ata National Park and Kara Koy

next.d: An Islamic village popular with local tourists and famous for its picturesque walnut tree forest.
Chon-Alai is a region Southwest of Osh containing the Lenina peak, the highest mountain in Kyrgyzstan.

intro: Kyrgyzstan (Kyrgyz and Russian: Кыргызстан), a Central Asian country, is often called as the "Switzerland" of Central Asia due to its mountainous terrain. The country offers breathtaking landscapes, including the Tien Shan Mountains, crystal-clear lakes such as Issyk-Kul and Song Kol, and beautiful valleys like the Ala-Archa National Park. These areas provide excellent hiking, trekking, horseback riding, and camping opportunities.

other.d: Lake and pearl of Central Asia, an enormous, crystal blue high alpine lake up in the Tian Shan Mountains.

x.intro: Issyk Kul (Kyrgyz: Ысык көл Ysyk Köl, Russian: Иссык-Куль) is a lake in Kyrgyzstan. The name refers both to the lake and the oblast (region) containing the lake. The region is centered around the massive Issyk Kul lake, which is the second largest alpine lake in the world. It is completely ringed by the massive snow-capped Tian Shan mountains that lie between 3,000 and 4,000 m.
x.safe: There are no lifeguards at any of the beaches. There are no nudist beaches and women being topless is quite rare, but local custom has no aversion to extremely skimpy swimsuits.

other.d: Issyk Kul's little cousin, far more remote, and many would say more beautiful as well.

x.around: There is nothing like public transportation on the circular road around the lake and the road is often in very bad shape. There are however some cars going on this road very often, you can try to hitchhike some of these to get where you need. Otherwise, you will have to walk a lot—the lake is quite large.

hidden.d: Maybe the only stone building near the lake. Very photogenic tomb at the shore.

x.intro: Song Kul is a high alpine lake in the mountains of the Naryn Region of Kyrgyzstan.

next.d: You probably came in from Kochkor. You can continue towards the Northwest from here by hiking, hitch-hiking or taxi.

other.d: One of the highlights of Kyrgyzstan with a beautiful lake, excellent hiking, diverse flora and fauna, picturesque mountains and much more.

x.around: To get to Chon-Alai take a marshrutka or shared taxi from Osh. But hitch-hiking might be the more economical and faster option.
x.intro: The Ferghana Valley stretches into several countries. This article covers the part in the southwest of Kyrgyzstan.

must.d: A historic site in the village of Safed Bulan where, according to legend, a woman named Bulan buried the heads of many of her Islamic brethren while they were busy praying and unexpectedly beheaded.

other.d: All that remains of the ancient Silk Road capital of Balasagun, a massive minaret standing alone on the step.
